This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 14-11-2024 at about 10.00 a.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-ET-1004 along with his friend Sekh Akbar, near Vinkatam Cafe,
Yogeswarnagar Cross, Bengaluru, slowly, cautiously, by observing traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, all of a sudden a BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-51-AJ-7673,
driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Altius Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ET-1004 himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and owner of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ET-1004 has got registered a false case against the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673, to get wrongful gain from the respondent No.2.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

It has neither adduced any evidence,
nor it has produced any document to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ET-1004 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-AJ-7673.
Even the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the above contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02- ET-1004 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of the road, near Venkatam Cafe, Lumbini Garden, Yogeshwarnagar Cross, Bengaluru, in between offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673 and ongoing motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ET-1004.
Further, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673.

Admittedly,
the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

sentences.text: No doubt, there is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, due to heavy pain he could not go to the police station on the same day to lodge the complaint and hence there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others,
reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.

Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
15.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in Ex.P.2 first information statement.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay in lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.18 & 33 x-rays,
Ex.P.19 OPD slip, Ex.P.20 discharge summary, Ex.P.24 inpatient record and Ex.P.32 clinical notes,
it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained traumatic right ankle bimalleolar fracture open Type 1 and left tibia shaft fracture.

The P.W.4, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.4 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 14-11-2024 at about 10.00 a.m., near Venkatam Cafe, Lumbini Garden, Yogeshwarnagar Cross, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AJ-7673 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained traumatic right ankle bimalleolar fracture open Type 1 and left tibia shaft fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
21. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card and driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.11 and 12.
As per Ex.P.11 and 12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 03-06-1985.
The accident has taken place on 14-11-2024 at about 10.00 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 39 years.

Further, the P.W.4, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered traumatic right ankle bimalleolar fracture open Type 1 and left tibia shaft fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, there is 38% physical disability to right upper limb, 40% physical disability to the left lower limb and 25% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.18 x- rays (total 10), Ex.P.19 OPD slip, Ex.P.20 discharge summary, Ex.P.24 inpatient record, Ex.P.32 clinical notes and Ex.P.33 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.4 in length
, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.4 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, fractures are united, implants are in situ, hip joint movement and muscle power are normal.

Further he has clearly admitted that, the range of movements will vary after removal of implant and the petitioner can perform his day to day activities and continue his avocation with some difficulties.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner,
duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
22. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Senior Technician at Safe Tech Electrical Solutions, Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.

In such circumstances,
the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

To substantiate the same he has produced identity card, letter dated 26-02-2025, reliving letter dated 27-02-2025, bank account statement, employee identity card, salary slips for the month of August-2024 to November-2024,
bank account statement, GST certificate, registration letter and relieving letter dated 27-02-2025,
which are marked as Ex.P.13, 15 to 17 and 26 to 31.
Further, he has also examined the authorised person/Project Manager of Safe Tech Electrical Solutions, Bengaluru, as P.W.3, to prove his avocation and income.

The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner was working as Senior Technical since 6 years in Safe Tech Electrial Solutions, Bengaluru and he was drawing salary of Rs.26,480/- per month.
As per Ex.P.27 salary slip for the month of November-2024, the petitioner was drawing salary of Rs.26,500/- per month.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner as on the date of accident is held at Rs.26,500/- per month, which comes to Rs.3,18,000/- per annum.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.30 resignation letter, due to grievous injuries sustained to his both legs, the petitioner has resigned from his job.
The Ex.P.31 relieving letter clearly speaks that, the resignation of the petitioner is accepted by his company and he has been relived from the job.

23. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 39 years is 15.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.3,18,000 X 15/100 X 15 = Rs.7,15,500/-.

31. Future medical expenses:
